title: feat: HashiCorp Vault as a read-only external credential store
body:
## Summary

Adds **HashiCorp Vault** as a third read-only external credential store for Agent Vault, alongside the built-in store and Infisical. A vault's credentials can now be sourced from a HashiCorp Vault KV mount, synced read-only and brokered to agents like any other credential.

It is a faithful mirror of the existing `internal/infisical` integration.

### Functional overview (how an operator uses it)
1. Configure the server: `VAULT_ADDR` plus an auth method — `VAULT_TOKEN`, or `VAULT_ROLE_ID` + `VAULT_SECRET_ID` for AppRole. (Standard `VAULT_NAMESPACE` / `VAULT_CACERT` / `VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY` are honored.)
2. Create a HashiCorp-backed vault, via CLI:
   ```
   agent-vault vault create my-app \
     --credential-store=hashicorp \
     --hashicorp-mount=secret \
     --hashicorp-path=agent-vault/demo \
     --hashicorp-kv-version=2
   ```
   …or via the web **New vault** form (HashiCorp Vault option + mount/path/KV-version fields).
3. The KV item's key/value pairs become the vault's credentials, polled read-only at the per-vault cadence and served through the broker. Rotate a secret in HashiCorp Vault → it propagates on the next sync (or **Manual sync**). Local mutations are rejected; HashiCorp Vault is the source of truth.

### Technical overview
- **`internal/hashicorp`** (new) — mirrors `internal/infisical`: auth-method detection (token / AppRole), a `vault/api` client (KV v1 + v2), and a per-vault `Syncer` that fetches, encrypts with the DEK, and replaces the cached credentials.
- **store** — migration `050` widens the `vault_credential_stores.kind` CHECK to allow `'hashicorp'`; adds the `CredentialStoreHashicorp` constant.
- **server** — a second sync worker; the shutdown drain now waits on **all** external-store syncers before wiping the DEK.
- **handlers** — `createExternalVault` and the manual-sync handler dispatch by kind; upstream topology (mount/path, sync errors, invalid-key names) is redacted from non-admin/owner viewers.
- **CLI** — `--credential-store=hashicorp` + `--hashicorp-mount/-path/-kv-version`.
- **web** — HashiCorp option + fields in the create-vault form.

### Dependency note — `github.com/hashicorp/vault/api`
This introduces `vault/api v1.23.0` (+ ~14 transitive deps). The code uses a thin slice (`DefaultConfig`, `NewClient`, `SetToken`/`SetNamespace`, `Logical().WriteWithContext` for AppRole login, `KVv1/KVv2.Get`), so a ~150-line `net/http` client is technically feasible. We chose the **official SDK** because it: correctly handles the standard `VAULT_*` env surface operators expect to "just work" (`VAULT_CACERT`/`VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY`/`VAULT_NAMESPACE`); unwraps the KV v2 `data`/`metadata` envelope (a footgun to reimplement); and provides retry/backoff + rootcert handling. This is consistent with the precedent (the Infisical store already depends on `infisical/go-sdk`). `go.mod`/`go.sum` are `go mod tidy`-clean. Happy to swap to a thin client as a follow-up if maintainers prefer.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI / build

## Test plan

- [x] Existing tests pass (`make test` — full `go test ./...` green, incl. `internal/mitm` e2e)
- [x] Added/updated tests for new behavior — unit (auth detection + AppRole login, config parse/validate/defaults, `stringValue` coercion, `Syncer` refresh/invalid-key/kind-filter), a hermetic integration test driving the **real `vault/api` client** against an `httptest` stub Vault (KV v1, KV v2, not-found — no Docker, runs in `make test`), and an **end-to-end test injecting a synced credential through the MITM proxy** (`internal/mitm/forward_hashicorp_test.go`).
- [x] Manual testing — ran a live HashiCorp Vault (Docker), seeded secrets, created the vault via **both CLI and the web form**, confirmed the synced values match upstream, exercised injection through the proxy, and verified rotation propagates after sync. (Happy to record a screen walkthrough if useful.)

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials in code — tokens/RoleID/SecretID read from env only; `.env.example` uses empty placeholders; secret values are never logged or returned (only key counts / scrubbed messages).
- [x] No new unauthenticated endpoints — reuses existing routes; external-store create is instance-owner-gated; the available-stores list is owner-gated.
- [x] Input validation on new API surfaces — `VaultConfig.Validate()` (mount/path/kv_version); poll-interval floor enforced server-side and via DB CHECK; CLI + web pre-validate.
- [x] Checked for OWASP top 10 — AppRole login sends structured params to a fixed path (no injection); upstream error bodies (which can embed `VAULT_ADDR`) are scrubbed to logs; `VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY` downgrade is surfaced as an auditable warning; synced values encrypted at rest with the DEK before persistence; UPPER_SNAKE_CASE key validation enforced on every fetched key.

title: Add GitHub App credential type for proxy-side installation token injection
body:
## Summary

Agent Vault should support GitHub App credentials as a first-class credential type, so proxy-only agents can access GitHub without ever receiving a GitHub token, private key, or PEM material.

## Problem

Today Agent Vault can inject static credentials and OAuth credentials at proxy time. That works for PATs, API keys, and OAuth access tokens, but GitHub App installation authentication has a different lifecycle:

1. Store GitHub App identity and private key.
2. Sign a short-lived GitHub App JWT.
3. Exchange it for an installation access token.
4. Inject that installation token into proxied GitHub API/git requests.
5. Refresh before expiry.

Without native support, users must either:

- give agents a token outside Agent Vault,
- store a static PAT instead of using GitHub App identity,
- or run a separate broker/rotator beside Agent Vault.

For security-sensitive agent workflows, the desired model is that the agent has only a proxy-role Agent Vault token. It can use allowed GitHub operations through the proxy, but cannot read or exfiltrate the GitHub App private key or derived installation token.

## Proposed Feature

Add a GitHub App credential type that can be referenced by services similarly to static/OAuth credentials.

The generated installation token should be cached server-side until near expiry and refreshed automatically. Proxy-role agents should never be able to read either the source private key or the derived installation token.

This should ideally work for both built-in Agent Vault credentials and Infisical-backed vaults, so teams can keep Infisical as the source of truth for the GitHub App private key while Agent Vault handles derived token minting and proxy-side injection.

title: feat(server): serve UI and API under a configurable URL path prefix (--ui-base-path)
body:
Closes #253

## Summary

Adds first-class support for serving the web UI (and `/v1` API) under a URL path prefix behind a reverse proxy — `agent-vault server --ui-base-path /vault` (env `AGENT_VAULT_UI_BASE_PATH`). Today this requires a content-rewriting proxy (`sub_filter` on the minified bundle, hand-injected router basepath, manual cache-busting) that silently breaks on every rebuild; see #253 for the full pain.

**Design — path passthrough, runtime injection:**

- The server mounts its entire surface under the prefix (outer mux + `http.StripPrefix`); the proxy forwards the path **unmodified**. `X-Forwarded-Prefix` is deliberately not honored — the prefix is part of the real request path. `GET /` redirects to the prefix; `GET /health` stays at the root for platform probes (and `--detach`'s readiness poll).
- Vite builds with relative asset URLs (`base: "./"`); `index.html` carries a `<base href="/" />` placeholder that the server rewrites **once at startup** ([internal/server/basepath.go](../blob/feat/ui-base-path/internal/server/basepath.go)). The SPA reads the `<base>` tag at boot to set TanStack Router's `basepath` and prefix all `/v1` calls — no inline script, so the `script-src 'self'` CSP is untouched, and one published image works for any prefix.
- Only the unhashed `index.html` ever varies; content-hashed assets are served byte-for-byte, keeping immutable caching valid. With the option unset, `index.html` is served byte-identical to the build output (regression-tested).
- Session cookies are scoped to `Path={prefix}/`; `s.baseURL` gets the prefix appended (no double-append) so invite emails, proposal approval links, OAuth redirect/redirect_uri, and the `av_addr` handed to agents all include it. The CLI already joins paths onto `--address`, so `--address https://host/vault` works as-is. The MITM ingress (separate listener) is unaffected.

**Drive-by fix:** the mux never routed `/fonts/` or `/favicon.*` — webfonts and favicons 404ed even at the domain root. Now served.

Most of the diff is tests, docs, and `package-lock.json` churn from adding vitest; the runtime change is ~130 lines of Go and ~40 lines of TS. Happy to split the vitest setup or the static-file fix into separate PRs if preferred.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Bug fix (`/fonts/`, `/favicon.*` 404)
- [x] Documentation

## Test plan

- [x] Existing tests pass (`make test` — full suite with `-race -count=1` and CI's stubbed-webdist setup; `golangci-lint` v2.11 clean for the changed code; `go mod tidy` no-op; `npm ci && npm run build` green)
- [x] Added/updated tests for new behavior
  - Go ([internal/server/basepath_test.go](../blob/feat/ui-base-path/internal/server/basepath_test.go)): `NormalizeBasePath` validation, `index.html` injection (incl. root-mode byte-identity), full-stack routing under the prefix (API + SPA + redirects + unprefixed-404 + root `/health`), cookie `Path` on login/logout, baseURL prefix-append; `--ui-base-path` flag smoke test in `cmd/cmd_test.go`
  - Web: vitest unit tests for base-href parsing and API URL joining (`npm test` in `web/`)
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

Ran the built binary with `--ui-base-path /vault` in a throwaway `$HOME` and verified with curl/CLI: index and deep SPA routes serve `<base href="/vault/">`; hashed JS/CSS, favicons, and fonts return 200 under the prefix; `/` → 302 `/vault/`; unprefixed `/v1/status` → 404; register → login sets `Path=/vault/`; vault list, credential set/list/delete, and scoped-token minting all work; agent-mode CLI works with `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=http://…/vault` (`vault discover`); `av_addr` comes back with the prefix. Root-mode and Vite dev server regression-checked the same way. Docs include a rewrite-free nginx location block ([docs/self-hosting/path-prefix.mdx](../blob/feat/ui-base-path/docs/self-hosting/path-prefix.mdx)) and a deployment verification checklist.

Note for operators: OAuth apps registered against a previously root-mounted instance need their redirect URI updated to include the prefix, since `redirect_uri` derives from the (now prefixed) base URL.

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials in code
- [x] No new unauthenticated endpoints (the prefix remounts existing routes; the only additions are two redirects and root `/health`, which already existed)
- [x] Input validation on new API surfaces (`NormalizeBasePath` rejects empty/`.`/`..` segments and `?`/`#`/whitespace; the value is operator-supplied config, not request data)
- [x] Checked for OWASP top 10 — the injected `<base href>` is built from the validated operator flag only, never from request input, so no header/URL-driven base-tag injection; CSP unchanged (`script-src 'self'`, no inline script); cookie scoping tightened to the prefix


### AI disclaimer

I used Claude Fable 5 for help with the development.

title: Support serving the web UI under a URL path prefix (e.g. /agent-vault/) behind a reverse proxy
body:
## Problem

The server assumes it is mounted at the domain root. Deployers who want Agent Vault on a shared domain under a sub-path (e.g. `https://example.com/agent-vault/`) currently have to use a content-rewriting reverse proxy. A working nginx config today needs all of the following `sub_filter` hacks against the built bundle:

- rewrite `href="/`, `src="/`, `action="/`, and `url(/` in HTML/CSS to the prefix
- rewrite API calls inside the minified JS bundle: `"/v1/`, `'/v1/`, and template-literal `\`/v1/` occurrences
- inject the router basepath by rewriting the minified TanStack Router init (e.g. `Lr({routeTree:` → `Lr({basepath:"<prefix>",routeTree:`), which breaks whenever a rebuild changes minified identifiers
- append a manual `?v=` cache-bust token to .js/.css references, because the rewritten content no longer matches the content-hashed immutable filenames

This is fragile by construction — every image release can silently break the basepath injection.

## Proposal

First-class support in the server:

- a `--ui-base-path` flag / `AGENT_VAULT_UI_BASE_PATH` env var, default "" = current root behavior unchanged
- the server serves UI **and** `/v1` API under the prefix; the proxy passes the path through unmodified (no rewriting)
- runtime injection: the server templates only the unhashed `index.html` (`<base href>`) at startup; the SPA derives its router basepath and API prefix from it, so one published image works for any prefix and hashed assets stay byte-identical for immutable caching
- cookie `Path`, login redirects, invite/approval links, OAuth redirects, and the `av_addr` handed to agents respect the prefix
- docs with a rewrite-free nginx location block

I have a working implementation with tests and docs; PR incoming.

title: feat: auto-detect and recommend hostnames from proxy traffic
body:
## Summary

Surfaces unmatched hostnames from recent failing proxy traffic so operators can quickly configure them as services, instead of manually figuring out hostnames.

Three pieces:

- **Hostname discovery**: new `GET /v1/vaults/{name}/discovered-hosts` endpoint queries `request_logs` for hosts that hit 401/403 or got proxy-denied (`no_match`), filters out hosts already covered by configured services (including wildcards), deduplicates ports, and ranks by most recent failure. Shows on the Services tab as a collapsible section with "Add as service" buttons, plus a count badge on the sidebar nav. Capped at 5 visible with "Show all (N)".

- **Auth detection**: best-effort detection of auth scheme (bearer, basic, api-key) from request headers in the MITM forward handler. Stored as `auth_scheme` + `auth_header` columns on `request_logs` (new migration). When adding a service from discovered hosts, the auth type tab and header field are pre-selected.

- **Credential-to-service suggestions**: on the Credentials tab, any credential matching a catalog template's `suggested_credential_key` that isn't used by any service shows a suggestion banner linking to the Services tab with the preset auto-applied.

title: deps: bump modernc.org/sqlite from 1.50.1 to 1.52.0

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
Bumps [modernc.org/sqlite](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite) from 1.50.1 to 1.52.0.
Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

  • 2026-06-11 v1.54.0:

    • Add netbsd/amd64 to the set of supported targets, resolving [GitLab issue #246](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/246). The lib/sqlite_netbsd_amd64.go that shipped previously was a stale old-generator transpile that no longer compiled (the mu.enter/mu.leave build break reported in #246); it is replaced by a fresh new-generator transpile of SQLite 3.53.2, consistent with every other platform. modernc.org/sqlite/vec (sqlite-vec) is now vendored and auto-registers on netbsd as well. The full test suite, including the pcache and vec packages and the -race concurrency test, passes on NetBSD 10.1 / Go 1.26.3. Note: correct operation requires the matching modernc.org/libc fix for the NetBSD mmap(2) PAD ABI — without it, concurrent WAL access faults (SIGBUS) in the WAL-index shared memory.
    • See [GitLab merge request #82](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/82), thanks Leonardo Taccari (@​iamleot) and Thomas Klausner (@wiz)!

  • 2026-06-10 v1.53.0:

    • Add a Go-facing wrapper for SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2. PageCache is the factory and Cache the per-database instance, both idiomatic Go interfaces; Page exposes the raw Buf and Extra pointers that SQLite reads through the C pcache contract. RegisterPageCache and MustRegisterPageCache install the module process-globally before the first sql.Open; subsequent Open calls are gated through a one-shot Xsqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2) so a too-late Register returns ErrPageCacheTooLate rather than silently falling through to the built-in pcache1. The binding owns the sqlite3_pcache_page stub and re-consults the implementation on every Fetch, reusing the stub only when the returned Page value is unchanged, which keeps a bounded/evicting purgeable cache safe by construction.
    • See [GitLab merge request #126](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/126), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add modernc.org/sqlite/pcache, the reference page-cache implementation that accompanies the #126 SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2 wrapper. pcache.New returns a *Pool satisfying the PageCache interface; register it once with sqlite.MustRegisterPageCache(pcache.New()) and every connection opened afterwards draws its pages from it. Each Pool.Create mints a fresh per-database Cache: a bounded, LRU-evicting page store that honours the PRAGMA cache_size soft cap and releases the least-recently-unpinned page when it must make room. Page memory — the Buf and Extra buffers SQLite reads through — is allocated with libc.Xmalloc/libc.Xcalloc and therefore lives off the Go heap, which keeps SQLite's interior pointer arithmetic on the page extras from tripping the race detector's checkptr enforcement. Pool.Stats reports aggregate lifetime counters (hits, misses, allocs, evictions, rekeys, truncates, caches) across every cache a Pool has created, so hit/miss/eviction behaviour is observable without instrumenting individual caches. Cross-connection page sharing is out of scope for now; each Create returns an independent per-database cache.
    • Validated end-to-end against the #126 stress workload (cache_size=16, 4000 BLOB rows with DELETE and incremental_vacuum, integrity_check clean under -race) and benchmarked for the memory-utilization goal tracked in [GitLab issue #204](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/204).
    • See [GitLab merge request #127](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/127), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add an opt-in _dqs DSN query parameter that disables SQLite's double-quoted string literal compatibility quirk on a per-connection basis. When _dqs=0 (or any strconv.ParseBool false value) is supplied, the driver calls sqlite3_db_config with SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DQS_DDL and SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DQS_DML set to off before any statement is prepared, so a double-quoted identifier that fails to resolve raises a parse error instead of silently falling back to a string literal. Absence of the parameter, or _dqs=1, leaves SQLite's default behavior unchanged; existing DSNs continue to work byte-for-byte. Resolves [GitLab issue #61](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/61).
    • See [GitLab merge request #128](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/128), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add an opt-in _error_rc DSN query parameter for clearer error reporting on open-time failures. When _error_rc=1 (or any strconv.ParseBool true value) is supplied, error strings synthesised from a (rc, db) pair only append sqlite3_errmsg(db) when sqlite3_extended_errcode(db) is consistent with the operation rc (full match first, primary code &0xff as fallback). On mismatch the canonical sqlite3_errstr(rc) is used alone, so an open-time SQLITE_CANTOPEN no longer carries the temporary handle's stale "out of memory" errmsg. Absence of the parameter, or _error_rc=0, preserves the legacy "errstr: errmsg" form byte-for-byte; existing callers that parse error strings are unaffected. The driver's *Error.Code() returns the same SQLite result code in both modes. Parsed before sqlite3_open_v2 so open-time errors are covered. Resolves [GitLab issue #230](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/230).
    • See [GitLab merge request #129](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/129), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-06-06 v1.52.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.2.
    • Add Backup.Remaining and Backup.PageCount, thin wrappers around the existing sqlite3_backup_remaining and sqlite3_backup_pagecount C symbols. Together they expose the per-Step progress counters that the underlying backup object already maintains, enabling progress reporting during online backups without dropping to modernc.org/sqlite/lib directly.
    • See [GitLab merge request #122](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/122), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Drop the redundant second copy in (*conn).columnText, the path that backs every Rows.Scan into a Go string for a TEXT column. The value's bytes are still copied once out of SQLite-owned memory into a fresh Go buffer; that buffer is then reinterpreted as the result string with unsafe.String rather than copied a second time by the implicit string([]byte) conversion. This removes one allocation per TEXT value per row and roughly halves the bytes allocated on that path; on the new BenchmarkColumnTextScan cases it is ~13–20% faster for payloads of 256 B and larger, with no measurable change for very short strings. Purely internal: no API or behavioral change, and the returned string never aliases SQLite's buffer.
    • See [GitLab merge request #123](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/123), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Cache each result column's declared type once per result set in newRows instead of recomputing it on every row. The TEXT branch of Rows.Next calls ColumnTypeDatabaseTypeName for every TEXT column on every row (independent of any DSN flag), which previously did a libc.GoString + strings.ToUpper each time; that lookup is now a single index into a cached, pre-uppercased []string, and ColumnTypeScanType reads the same cache and drops its per-call strings.ToLower. The declared type is fixed for the lifetime of a prepared statement, so the C round-trip is paid once per column rather than once per column per row, removing exactly 1 alloc + 8 B per TEXT column per row from the Next hot path. The new BenchmarkTextToTimeScan cases show ~7% faster on a 1000-row DATETIME SELECT under _texttotime=1. Purely internal: ColumnTypeDatabaseTypeName and ColumnTypeScanType return identical values, no API or behavioral change.
    • See [GitLab merge request #124](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/124), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Cache, per result column, the parseTimeFormats index that first parsed a TEXT-stored DATE/DATETIME/TIMESTAMP value, and try that format first on later rows instead of re-walking the list from the top. (*conn).parseTime previously ran time.Parse down the format list on every such row; for the canonical SQLite TEXT datetime format every row paid two failed time.Parse attempts — each allocating a *time.ParseError — before the match. On a 1000-row DATETIME TEXT SELECT this cuts ~50% of allocs/op and ~57% of B/op and is ~37% faster. The fall-through chain is preserved exactly: the seven formats are mutually exclusive, so the cached hint can never select a different match than the in-order scan, and the parsed driver.Value is identical to before. Purely internal: no API or behavioral change.
    • See [GitLab merge request #125](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/125), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-05-28 v1.51.0:

    • Pool the []driver.Value slice passed to scalar/aggregate UDF callbacks and to vtab Filter/Insert/Update callbacks, eliminating the dominant per-row allocation on UDF-heavy queries. Benchmarks on a 1000-row, 3-arg noop scalar UDF show ~40% fewer bytes/op and ~15% fewer allocs/op.
    • Document the matching "arguments are not valid past return" contract on vtab.Cursor.Filter and vtab.Updater.Insert/Update, consistent with the existing rule for FunctionImpl.Scalar / AggregateFunction.Step / WindowInverse.
    • Resolves [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #114](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/114), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add FileControl.FileControlDataVersion, a wrapper around SQLITE_FCNTL_DATA_VERSION for observing pager-cache data-version changes, including those made on the same connection. Useful as a primitive for application-level cache invalidation.
    • Exposed via the idiomatic database/sql escape hatch (*sql.Conn).Raw(), consistent with the existing FileControlPersistWAL.
    • See [GitLab merge request #115](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/115), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a regression where in-memory connections (:memory:, file::memory:, shared-cache memory URIs) were discarded by database/sql after a context-cancelled query, taking the entire in-memory store with them. The fix for #198 had added an sqlite3_is_interrupted check to the connection validator that mistakenly applied to in-memory connections too, re-introducing the bug originally fixed by !74. File-backed connections keep the existing behaviour and are still discarded after an interrupt.
    • Resolves [GitLab issue #196](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/196). See [GitLab merge request #116](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/116), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add an opt-in FunctionImpl.VolatileArgs flag that hands TEXT and BLOB arguments to scalar and aggregate UDF callbacks as zero-copy views (unsafe.String/unsafe.Slice) over SQLite's own value buffers, eliminating the per-argument libc.GoString/make([]byte) copy that the #226 slice-pooling left as the remaining per-row allocation. On the same 1000-row, 3-arg (INTEGER/TEXT/BLOB) noop scalar UDF this removes a further ~35% of allocs/op and ~11% of bytes/op on top of #226.
    • The views are valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past return or across rows; a callback that needs to keep a value must copy it. With VolatileArgs unset (the default) arguments keep the existing copied, caller-owned semantics, so the flag is fully backward compatible; it has no effect on integer, float, time, or NULL arguments.
    • See [GitLab merge request #120](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/120), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Extend the opt-in VolatileArgs zero-copy TEXT/BLOB argument access from #120 to the virtual-table Cursor.Filter (xFilter) and Updater.Insert/Update (xUpdate) callbacks. A vtab.Module opts in by implementing the new optional vtab.VolatileArgsOpter interface (VolatileArgs() bool); the flag is read once at module registration and shared by every table created from it. On a vtab call carrying one TEXT and one BLOB argument this removes 2 allocs/op (one libc.GoString, one make([]byte)) on each of the Filter and Update paths.
    • The same safety contract as #120 applies: the views are valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past return or across rows; a callback that needs to keep a value must copy it. Modules that do not implement VolatileArgsOpter (the default for all existing modules) are byte-for-byte unchanged, and the flag has no effect on integer, float, time, or NULL arguments.
    • See [GitLab merge request #121](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/121), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-05-10 v1.50.1:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.1.

  • 2026-04-24 v1.50.0:

    • Upgrade to sqlite-vec v0.1.9.
    • Introduce ColumnInfo, enabling dynamic query builders and ORMs to retrieve underlying SQLite C-API metadata (OriginName, TableName, DatabaseName, and DeclType).

... (truncated)

title: feat: add OAuth credential type with Connect flow and Token Upload
body:
## Summary

Adds OAuth 2.0 as a credential type alongside static credentials. Two modes:

- **Connect flow**: admin registers an OAuth app with the provider, enters client ID/secret in Agent Vault, clicks Connect, and completes the consent flow. Agent Vault handles the redirect, callback, and token exchange (Authorization Code + PKCE).
- **Token Upload**: admin pastes tokens obtained from an external source (e.g., `~/.claude/.credentials.json` from Claude Code). If a refresh token is provided, it's validated immediately against the provider's token endpoint.

The proxy injects OAuth tokens the same way as static credentials. Tokens are refreshed automatically when they near expiry.

- Migration 048 adds `type` column to credentials and two new tables (`credential_oauth`, `credential_oauth_states`)

title: fix(auth): prevent account takeover via unverified registration password overwrite
body:
## Summary

The registration handler was overwriting an inactive user's password when someone re-registered with the same email, while old verification codes remained valid. An attacker could replace a victim's password before they verified, then log in once the victim activated the account.

- Remove the `UpdateUserPassword` call on re-registration of inactive accounts — only resend a verification code
- Unify response messages and the `email_sent` field across all registration branches to prevent account-state enumeration
- Extract the uniform message to a `registerUniformMessage` const to prevent drift
- Bump `TierAuth` rate limit from 10 → 50 per 5 min — teams behind corporate NAT were hitting the ceiling during normal use
- Fix login handler double-counting the IP budget (`Allow` → `Check` for the IP key, since `ipAuth` middleware already recorded it — same pattern as the MITM proxy fix in #226)

title: feat: flush MITM responses per-chunk for live streaming (git clone, SSE)
body:
## Summary

Streaming responses (git clone pack data, SSE event streams) were buffered by Go's `ResponseWriter` until the internal 4 KB buffer filled or the handler returned. Upstream chunk boundaries collapsed into a single blob — git's sideband parser stalled, SSE events arrived late, and any chunk-boundary-sensitive protocol broke. On top of that, the CONNECT tunnel's `WriteTimeout: 5 * time.Minute` killed any transfer that took longer than 5 minutes to stream.

Concrete failure: `git clone` of `microsoft/TypeScript` through the proxy died with `fatal: early EOF` / `fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`. Same root cause as external draft PR #197.

**Per-chunk flushing**

Wraps the `ResponseWriter` in a `flushingWriter` that calls `http.Flusher.Flush()` after every successful `Write`. `io.Copy` uses a 32 KB buffer, so this flushes every ≤32 KB — upstream chunk boundaries reach the client immediately instead of coalescing. Applied to both the HTTP forward path (`forward.go`) and the WebSocket non-101 fallback path (`websocket.go`).

For non-streaming responses (single JSON body with `Content-Length`), this is effectively a no-op — `io.Copy` does one `Write` and one `Flush`, same as before.

**CONNECT tunnel WriteTimeout raised to 30 minutes**

The previous 5-minute `WriteTimeout` on the CONNECT tunnel's `http.Server` was an absolute deadline from request-header-read to response-complete. Any streaming response >5 minutes was killed. Raised to 30 minutes to cover realistic long-running transfers. Slow-loris defense is preserved by `ReadHeaderTimeout` (10s) and `ReadTimeout` (60s) on the request side, `IdleTimeout` (2 min) between requests, and the upstream transport's `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (5 min) for stalled upstreams.

**WebSocket oversized-frame substitution warning**

Added `slog.Warn` when a WebSocket text frame exceeds the 1 MB substitution buffer (`maxWSSubstitutionPayload`) and substitutions are configured. The existing fragmentation case already warned; the size case silently passed through.

Supersedes #197.

title: refactor(skills): make agent-vault feel seamless by consolidating to a single reactive skill
body:
## Summary

Agents were becoming overly aware of Agent Vault and prompting users unnecessarily about proxy routing and credential checking. Someone in the wild mentioned "I often need to remind it that it's the source to use" — the opposite of what we want. The proxy is transparent; agents shouldn't need to think about it.

The root cause was two verbose skill files that instructed agents to proactively run `discover` before every API call ("CRITICAL: Always Check Agent Vault First"). This made agents paranoid and chatty — checking AV, mentioning it to users, asking for confirmation before making requests that would just work.

**What changed:**

Rewrote `skill_cli.md` to be reactive instead of proactive. The agent no longer runs discover before every call. Instead it just makes requests normally. If they work (most will — the proxy injects credentials transparently), great. If they fail with 401/403, the skill teaches how to create a proposal.

Key info moved into the skill description (the part agents always see, even before loading the full skill):
- Placeholder API keys work because a proxy injects real credentials on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames
- If you don't have a key, set a dummy value and make the call anyway
- When writing code, make sure HTTP clients pick up `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` from the environment

Deleted `skill_http.md` entirely. It taught agents how the proxy works (env vars, CONNECT tunnels, CA trust) — implementation details agents don't need. One skill is enough.

Removed the HTTP skill embed, install path, serve endpoint (`/v1/skills/http`), and all references across code, tests, and docs.

title: feat: configurable MITM response/request body size caps
body:
## Summary

The MITM proxy hardcoded a 100 MB response body cap (`MaxResponseBytes`) and a 64 MB request body cap (`MaxProxyBodyBytes`) that silently truncated large transfers. `git clone` of any repo with >100 MB of history (TypeScript, React, Kubernetes, most company monorepos) failed with a confusing `early EOF` / `unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` error. The server logged `status=200` with no warning — users had no way to tell the proxy was at fault.

Confirmed by reproduction: cloning `microsoft/TypeScript` through the proxy truncated at exactly 104,857,600 bytes (the hardcoded limit). Same root cause reported in #210 and external draft PR #198.

**Response body cap: now unlimited by default**

Response bodies are streamed with a 32 KB `io.Copy` buffer — no OOM risk regardless of size. The old 100 MB cap only broke legitimate transfers. Default is now `0` (unlimited). Operators who want a bandwidth guard can set `--max-response-bytes` / `AGENT_VAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`.

When a limit IS configured:
- **Known oversize** (`Content-Length > limit`): returns 502 Bad Gateway with `X-Agent-Vault-Proxy-Error` and a clear JSON error before streaming any body
- **Mid-stream discovery** (chunked, hits limit): aborts the connection via `http.ErrAbortHandler` — client sees a connection reset, not silently corrupted data

This follows the industry standard (nginx, Squid, Envoy): reject, never silently truncate.

**Request body cap: configurable, default 1 GiB**

Raised from 64 MB to 1 GiB via `--max-request-bytes` / `AGENT_VAULT_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`. Fixes `git push` of large repos and bulk file uploads that previously hit 413.

**OOM fix: conditional body materialization**

Previously, every request body was fully buffered in RAM by `MaterializeRequestBody` — up to the body cap per concurrent request. Now:

- **Known-length bodies without body substitutions** (the common case: git, file uploads, API calls): streamed directly to the upstream without materialization. `Content-Length` is forwarded from the original request.
- **Unknown-length (chunked) or body-substitution bodies**: materialized as before, but capped at 64 MB (`MaxMaterializeBytes`) regardless of the request cap. Body substitutions target small API payloads (JSON, form-encoded), never large file uploads.

The reorder is safe: `Inject()` takes `(ctx, vaultID, host, path)` — no body dependency — so it moves before materialization. `HasBodySubstitutions()` (new helper) checks the substitution surfaces before deciding the path.

**Observability**

Both the 502 rejection and mid-stream abort paths log `slog.Warn` with host, path, bytes streamed, and the configured limit. Previously: zero logging on truncation.

title: fix: only count proxy auth failures against TierAuth rate limit
body:
## Summary

Remote agents (Docker, VPS) get 429'd after ~10 CONNECT tunnels because every connection eats from the AUTH rate limit budget (10 per 5 min per IP) — even when the agent has valid credentials. Client libraries surface this as a generic "connection error" with no hint it's a rate limit.

The AUTH rate limit was designed for brute-force protection on login. But the MITM proxy checked it on every CONNECT/forward request before running auth, so legitimate agents burned through the budget just by connecting to a few services on startup.

**What changed:**

Added a read-only `Check()` to the rate limiter alongside the existing `Allow()`. The proxy now peeks before auth and only records when auth fails. Successful connections skip AUTH entirely — they're already covered by the PROXY tier.

Also updated the AUTH tier descriptions across Go comments, frontend tooltip, and docs. Removed the "disable rate limiting" workaround from the Hermes-on-VPS guide since it was a bandaid for this bug.

Closes #224

title: feat: add body and websocket substitution surfaces
body:
## Summary

Two new substitution surfaces that let agents send credentials in HTTP request bodies and WebSocket frames — not just headers, paths, and query strings.

**1. Body substitution (`"in": ["body"]`)**

Some APIs send credentials in the POST body instead of headers. The most common case is OAuth `client_secret_post` — used by GitHub, Slack, Spotify, Google, Microsoft, and AWS Cognito for token exchanges. Slack's `@slack/web-api` also puts the bot token in the body on `auth.test` calls, which broke Bolt-based agents (#208).

- Reads the request body, replaces placeholders, updates `Content-Length`
- Encoding-aware per `Content-Type`: URL-encodes for `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (via `mime.ParseMediaType` to handle `; charset=utf-8`), JSON-string-escapes for `application/json`, skips `multipart/*`, raw replacement for everything else
- Skips compressed bodies (`Content-Encoding` set) with a debug log
- Body is already materialized in memory by `MaterializeRequestBody` — no extra buffering

**2. WebSocket frame substitution (`"in": ["websocket"]`)**

Discord's Gateway sends the bot token inside a JSON WebSocket frame (Identify and Resume events). There is no alternative auth mechanism — no header, no query param, no bearer token during the upgrade handshake. The token must be in the frame body. Reported in #209.

- Parses individual WebSocket frames per RFC 6455 on the client→server direction only
- Unmasks text frames, applies `strings.ReplaceAll` for each placeholder, re-masks with `crypto/rand`
- Handles all three length encodings (7-bit, 16-bit, 64-bit) including transitions when substitution changes payload size
- Passes through binary frames, control frames (close/ping/pong), compressed frames (RSV1), and fragmented frames untouched
- 1MB payload cap — oversized frames stream through via `io.CopyN` without buffering
- Rejects frames with MSB set on 64-bit length (RFC 6455 §5.2) to prevent `int64` overflow
- Strips `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` from the upgrade handshake when websocket substitutions are active, preventing `permessage-deflate` negotiation that would make frames opaque
- When no websocket substitutions are configured, the existing blind byte copier runs — zero overhead

**Configuration**

Existing model, two new options in the surface selector. `body` and `websocket` are opt-in (not in `DefaultSubstitutionSurfaces`).

Discord example:
```json
{
  "name": "discord-gateway",
  "host": "gateway.discord.gg",
  "auth": {"type": "passthrough"},
  "substitutions": [
    {"key": "DISCORD_TOKEN", "placeholder": "__discord_token__", "in": ["websocket"]}
  ]
}
```

Slack/OAuth example:
```json
{
  "name": "slack-api",
  "host": "slack.com",
  "auth": {"type": "bearer", "token": "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"},
  "substitutions": [
    {"key": "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN", "placeholder": "__slack_bot_token__", "in": ["header", "body"]}
  ]
}
```

**What was tested**

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Unit: body substitution (12 tests) | form-encoded with special chars, JSON with `"` and `\`, multipart skip, charset params, nil/empty body, scoping |
| Unit: WebSocket frames (8 tests) | text frame substitution, binary pass-through, close/ping/pong, length encoding 7-bit→16-bit transition, oversized frame stream-through, filter helper |
| Unit: validation | body/websocket accepted, unknown surfaces rejected |
| E2E: body via httpbin | form-encoded and JSON bodies through MITM proxy, placeholder replaced, Content-Length correct, scoping verified (header untouched when only body declared) |
| E2E: WebSocket via real Discord Gateway | Go test client → proxy → gateway.discord.gg: Identify with placeholder → substituted → Discord sent READY |
| E2E: Hermes + Discord in Docker | Full Hermes gateway running in Docker through Agent Vault proxy. Bot connected to Discord (`av-seb#9550`), received messages, called Anthropic API (also proxied), responded in Discord. All credentials injected by Agent Vault — agent container held only placeholders. |
| SDK tests (95 tests) | All pass |
| Full suite (`make test`) | All pass |

Closes #209

title: AUTH rate limit on CONNECT tunnels breaks remote agents (Docker, VPS)
body:
## Problem

Remote agents (Docker containers, VPS deployments) get `429 Too Many Requests` on the MITM proxy after ~10 HTTPS connections, blocking all proxy traffic for 5 minutes. The error surfaces in client libraries as `Connection error` or `APIConnectionError` with no indication it's a rate limit, making it very hard to diagnose.

## Root Cause

`internal/mitm/connect.go:53-57` — every CONNECT tunnel through the MITM proxy counts against the `TierAuth` rate limit (10 per 5 min per IP). The check runs **before** proxy authentication:

```go
func (p *Proxy) handleConnect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // Gate before ParseProxyAuth + session lookup so a bad-auth flood
    // can't burn CPU. Per-IP on the raw TCP peer, shared with the
    // TierAuth budget. Loopback is exempt — see isLoopbackPeer.
    if p.rateLimit != nil && !isLoopbackPeer(r) {
        if d := p.rateLimit.Allow(ratelimit.TierAuth, mitmIPKey(r)); !d.Allow {
            ratelimit.WriteDenial(w, d, "Too many CONNECT attempts")
            return  // ← 429 here, never reaches authentication on line 74
        }
    }

    // ... 15 lines later ...

    // Authenticate the CONNECT request via Proxy-Authorization
    token, hint, err := brokercore.ParseProxyAuth(r)  // line 74
```

The `TierAuth` tier was designed to prevent login brute-force (10 attempts per 5 min is appropriate for password guessing). But CONNECT tunnels also count against this same budget.

**Loopback (127.0.0.1) is already exempt** — the code acknowledges that agents "legitimately open dozens of CONNECTs on startup" (comment on line 29-35). But remote agents (Docker containers, VPS deployments) are not exempt, and they hit the exact same problem.

## How an Agent Exhausts the Budget

A typical agent (e.g., Hermes with Discord) opens these CONNECT tunnels on startup:

1. `discord.com` — REST API login
2. `gateway.discord.gg` — WebSocket connection
3. `api.anthropic.com` — main LLM client
4. `api.anthropic.com` — auxiliary client (title generation)
5. `api.anthropic.com` — auxiliary client (summarization)
6. Any reconnects or retries from transient errors

That's 5-6 tunnels immediately. One user message triggers a few more (streaming creates new connections in some HTTP clients). After 10 total, the proxy returns 429 on every new CONNECT for the remaining 5-minute window.

## What the User Sees

The 429 happens at the CONNECT level (before TLS), so HTTP client libraries don't see it as a rate limit — they see a failed tunnel establishment. Examples:

- **Python (httpx/Anthropic SDK):** `anthropic.APIConnectionError: Connection error.`
- **Python (aiohttp/discord.py):** `aiohttp.ClientHttpProxyError: 429, message='Too Many Requests'`
- **Go:** `bad gateway` or connection refused

No `Retry-After` header reaches the application layer because the CONNECT response is consumed by the HTTP client's proxy handling, not exposed to the application.

## Discovered During

Testing the body + WebSocket substitution feature (#209) with Hermes + Discord in Docker. Took several hours to diagnose because the error message gives no hint it's a rate limit. The Hermes-on-VPS guide already tells users to disable rate limiting entirely as a workaround, which confirms this is a known pain point.

## Suggested Fix

**Minimal (recommended):** Don't count CONNECT tunnels against `TierAuth` when proxy authentication succeeds. The `TierProxy` tier (20 req/s, burst 200, 64 concurrent) already rate-limits authenticated proxy traffic appropriately. The AUTH check on CONNECT should only fire when authentication **fails** — that's the actual brute-force vector it was designed to prevent.

Concretely, in `connect.go`: move the `TierAuth` rate limit check to after `ParseProxyAuth` and `ResolveForProxy`, and only apply it on auth failure. On auth success, skip the AUTH tier entirely.

**Broader improvement (optional, can be a follow-up):** Consider removing `TierProxy` and `TierAuthed` from the default profile entirely. Agent Vault is typically deployed on private networks where the agent already authenticates with a token — rate limiting authenticated traffic protects against a threat that doesn't exist in most deployments. Keep `TierAuth` on login/register (real brute-force risk if API is internet-exposed), `TierGlobal` as a server-wide safety net, and `TierVerifyFail` for verification codes. Operators who want tighter limits can switch to the `strict` profile.

## Current Rate Limit Tiers (for context)

| Tier | Where | What it limits | Default | Issue? |
|------|-------|---------------|---------|--------|
| **AUTH** | API + Proxy CONNECT | Login, register, forgot-password, AND CONNECT tunnels | 10 per 5 min per IP | **Yes — breaks remote agents** |
| **PROXY** | Proxy only | Forwarded requests after authentication | 20 req/s, burst 200, 64 concurrent | No, but unnecessary for private networks |
| **AUTHED** | API only | Authenticated API calls (proposals, vaults, credentials) | 10 req/s, burst 240 | No, but unnecessary — session is the protection |
| **GLOBAL** | Everything | Server-wide backstop | 2000 req/s, 512 concurrent | No — keep as safety net |
| **VERIFY_FAIL** | API only | Bad verification/reset code guesses | 10 bad guesses, code burned | No — keep for brute-force protection |

## Workaround

Until fixed, users can crank up the AUTH tier via the admin API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:14321/v1/admin/settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate_limit": {"overrides": {"AUTH": {"window": "1m", "max": 10000}}}}'
```

Or disable rate limiting entirely (what the Hermes guide currently recommends):

```bash
# Via UI: Manage Instance → Rate Limiting → Off
# Via env: set profile to "off" in admin settings
```

## Files to Look At

- `internal/mitm/connect.go` — CONNECT handler, lines 49-58 (the rate limit check), lines 74-83 (authentication)
- `internal/mitm/forward.go` — forward-proxy handler has the same pattern (search for `TierAuth`)
- `internal/ratelimit/` — tier definitions, defaults, algorithms
- `internal/server/ratelimit_settings.go` — how settings are stored and applied

title: deps: bump vite to 8 and @vitejs/plugin-react to 6 in /web
body:
Combines dependabot PRs #222 and #219, which cannot pass CI independently: vite 8 requires `@vitejs/plugin-react` >= 6, and plugin-react 6 requires vite >= 8. Their peer ranges interlock, so each PR alone fails `npm ci` with ERESOLVE.

Bumps both together:
- `vite` ^6.4.2 -> ^8.0.15
- `@vitejs/plugin-react` ^4.4.1 -> ^6.0.2

`@tailwindcss/vite@4.3.0` already allows vite ^8 in its peer range. Frontend build (`tsc && vite build`) verified locally on Node 20; CI builds on Node 22.

Closes #222
Closes #219

title: feat(run): add OpenClaw/Codex support, remove proxy TLS wrapping
body:
## Summary

Three related changes that fix agent compatibility and simplify the proxy architecture:

**1. OpenClaw support for `agent-vault run`**

OpenClaw's proxy system (Proxyline) ignores standard `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`. Without explicit support, `agent-vault run -- openclaw gateway run` silently bypassed the proxy for most traffic.

- Set `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` alongside standard proxy env vars so Proxyline picks it up
- Auto-configure `proxy.enabled` and `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` via `openclaw config set` (10s timeout, conditional success message, revert commands printed)
- Add `openclaw` to `knownAgents` for skill auto-installation

**2. Remove TLS wrapping from the MITM proxy listener**

The proxy listener was TLS-wrapped (`https://` scheme). This is non-standard — forward proxies listen on plain HTTP, with TLS only inside CONNECT tunnels. The wrapping caused two client compatibility issues:

- `curl` has no env var for proxy CA trust (`--proxy-cacert` only)
- Codex's WebSocket transport (tokio-tungstenite) rejects `https://` proxy URLs entirely, causing a 5-retry error storm before HTTP fallback (#194)

The control plane (14321) was already plain HTTP with the same token in cleartext. The TLS on the proxy added no security — an attacker on the network could get the token from the control plane regardless. Removing it aligns both to the same trust model and fixes all client compatibility issues.

**3. Fix control plane calls routing through the MITM proxy**

Control plane calls (discover, proposals, sessions) to `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` were going through the MITM proxy when the AV host wasn't in `NO_PROXY`. On non-localhost deployments (Docker, VPS), netguard blocked the private IP with a 502. Two fixes:

- Add the AV host to `NO_PROXY` in `BuildProxyEnv` for child processes
- Add a custom `Proxy` function on `httpClient` that skips the proxy for requests matching `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR`, falling through to `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` for everything else. This handles runtimes like OpenClaw whose Proxyline clears `NO_PROXY`.

**What was tested**

End-to-end credential injection in Docker (separate containers, private network, zero credentials on the agent):

| Agent | Provider API | HTTP Tool | curl | Proposals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | ✅ `[ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]` | ✅ `[TEST_KEY]` | ✅ `[TEST_KEY]` | ✅ |
| Codex | ✅ WebSocket 101, `[OPENAI_API_KEY]` | N/A | ✅ | ✅ |
| OpenClaw | ✅ `[ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]` | ✅ `[TEST_KEY]` | ✅ `[TEST_KEY]` | ✅ (Telegram) |

Additional: invalid credential → Anthropic rejects, restored → works. Codex zero WebSocket errors (was the original bug in #194).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / build

## Test plan

- [x] Existing tests pass (`make test`)
- [x] Added/updated tests for new behavior
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials in code
- [x] No new unauthenticated endpoints
- [x] Input validation on new API surfaces
- [x] Checked for OWASP top 10 (injection, XSS, etc.)

title: feat(run): add OpenClaw support for agent-vault run
body:
## Summary

OpenClaw's proxy system (Proxyline) does not use standard `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables. It requires `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` to activate managed proxy routing, plus two config settings (`proxy.enabled` and `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy`) that control which traffic tiers are covered.

Without these, `agent-vault run -- openclaw gateway run` appeared to work but silently bypassed the proxy for most traffic — provider API calls went direct, `web_fetch` tool calls went direct, and only a narrow set of gateway-internal HTTP (model discovery) was routed.

**What was the issue**

The existing quickstart docs for OpenClaw were untested. They claimed `agent-vault run` would route OpenClaw's traffic through Agent Vault via `HTTPS_PROXY`, but OpenClaw ignores those env vars for its managed proxy system. End-to-end testing against a live OpenClaw instance with Telegram and Anthropic revealed multiple gaps:

1. Proxyline requires `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` — standard proxy env vars are not read.
2. Proxyline requires `proxy.enabled: true` in OpenClaw's config — the env var alone is not enough.
3. The `web_fetch` tool has its own DNS-pinning security and requires a separate opt-in (`tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy: true`).
4. `curl` child processes could not verify the HTTPS proxy's TLS certificate because `curl` has no env var for proxy CA trust (only `--proxy-cacert`).
5. The MITM proxy's `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (30s) raced with Telegram's `getUpdates` long-poll (also 30s), causing intermittent 502s that crashed the Telegram channel.

**What we chose to fix**

- Set `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` alongside standard proxy env vars in `BuildProxyEnv` so Proxyline picks it up.
- Add `openclaw` to `knownAgents` for skill auto-installation.
- Auto-configure OpenClaw via `openclaw config set` when detected — sets `proxy.enabled` and `useTrustedEnvProxy` so no manual config editing is needed.
- Write `~/.curlrc` with `proxy-cacert` pointing at the MITM CA so `curl` child processes trust the HTTPS proxy without `--proxy-cacert` on every command or system CA store modification.
- Increase `ResponseHeaderTimeout` from 30s to 5 minutes to support long-polling services like Telegram.

**Alternatives considered**

- Installing the MITM CA into the system trust store (`update-ca-certificates`) — works but requires root and modifies global state. The `.curlrc` approach is non-invasive and doesn't need root.
- Adding a plain HTTP (non-TLS) proxy mode — would eliminate the proxy CA issue entirely, but the proxy URL contains the auth token which needs TLS protection for remote deployments.
- OpenClaw's `SecretRef` exec provider for credential resolution at activation time — would put real credentials in OpenClaw's memory, defeating the purpose of Agent Vault.

**Persistent side effects**

`agent-vault run` uses `syscall.Exec` (replaces the process), so there is no cleanup on exit. Two things persist that other agents don't have:

- OpenClaw config: `proxy.enabled` and `useTrustedEnvProxy` — breaks standalone `openclaw gateway run` until reverted. Revert commands are printed at startup and documented in the quickstart.
- `~/.curlrc`: a `proxy-cacert` line is appended. Harmless without `HTTPS_PROXY` set (curl ignores it). Never cleaned up, same as skill files for other agents.

This matches the existing pattern — skills are installed permanently for all agents, never removed.

**What was tested**

End-to-end credential injection verified in Docker (two containers on a private network, zero credentials on the agent machine):

- Anthropic API calls: dummy key on agent, real key injected by Agent Vault → Claude responds ✓
- Telegram Bot API: placeholder token substituted in URL path → bot authenticated and responsive ✓
- `web_fetch` tool: request catcher shows `Authorization: Bearer secret-12345` injected ✓
- `curl` child process: same credential injection via `.curlrc` proxy CA trust ✓
- Invalid credential test: changed AV credential to invalid → Anthropic rejects with `invalid x-api-key` ✓
- Restored credential → works again ✓

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / build

## Test plan

<!-- How did you verify this works? -->

- [x] Existing tests pass (`make test`)
- [x] Added/updated tests for new behavior
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials in code
- [x] No new unauthenticated endpoints
- [x] Input validation on new API surfaces
- [x] Checked for OWASP top 10 (injection, XSS, etc.)

title: run: loopback TLS bridge for clients that reject https:// proxy URLs
body:
## Summary

Adds a per-child loopback TLS terminator (`internal/proxybridge`) so agents whose HTTP/proxy libraries reject `https://`-scheme `HTTPS_PROXY` URLs can still route through Agent Vault's TLS-wrapped MITM proxy.

**Motivating case:** Codex's Responses WebSocket transport (OpenAI's fork of `tokio-tungstenite`) only accepts `http://`/`socks5://`/`socks5h://` proxy URLs and rejects `https://` at parse time, so every `agent-vault run -- codex ...` printed six `Proxy URL scheme not supported` errors and triggered a retry storm before falling back to the HTTPS Responses API. See #194.

## How it works

In `auto` mode (default), agents flagged in the `knownAgents` table (`needsTLSBridge`) get a loopback listener on `127.0.0.1:<random>`; each connection is spliced over TLS to the real MITM proxy, and the child's `HTTP(S)_PROXY` is rewritten to `http://...@127.0.0.1:<port>`. Only **Codex** auto-enables today. Flags: `--tls-bridge=auto|always|never`, env `AGENT_VAULT_TLS_BRIDGE`.

Bridge mode swaps `syscall.Exec` for `os/exec.Cmd` (with explicit SIGINT/TERM/HUP/QUIT forwarding + exit-code propagation) because the bridge goroutine must outlive the call. Non-bridge agents keep the original exec path unchanged.

## Security invariant

`Proxy-Authorization` stays TLS-encrypted on the wire end-to-end — the agent↔broker hop is unchanged. Cleartext is bounded to loopback inside the agent's own netns; the dialer pins the MITM CA with correct SNI, `MinVersion: TLS1.2`, no `InsecureSkipVerify`. Listener binds `127.0.0.1` only (pinned by test).

## Review notes / open questions

- [ ] Threat-model wording assumes per-container loopback, but the **default `host` mode** uses the host's shared loopback — tighten wording.
- [ ] Verify behavior under `--isolation=container` (host-loopback bridge may be unreachable from the container netns).
- [ ] Loopback relay is unauthenticated and spawns unbounded goroutines (local-only; broker auth still required).
- [ ] `NO_PROXY=localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` proxy host.
- [ ] Silent error swallowing in `handle`/`acceptLoop`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/proxybridge/...` passes under `-race`
- [x] End-to-end in Docker: `codex exec` with zero WSS errors; interactive Ctrl+C exits cleanly; unflagged binaries keep `https://` proxy unchanged
- [ ] `/security-review`
- [ ] `/code-review`

Closes #194.

title: Support explicit WebSocket frame substitutions for credentials in post-upgrade protocols
body:
# Support explicit WebSocket frame substitutions for credentials in post-upgrade protocols

## Problem

Agent Vault substitutions currently work for HTTP request surfaces (`path`, `query`, `header`) before a request is forwarded. This works for REST APIs and for WebSocket handshake metadata, but it does not work for credentials sent inside WebSocket message frames after the HTTP upgrade.

This breaks Discord Gateway auth for Hermes Agent when the Discord bot token is stored in Agent Vault as a substitution placeholder.

**Discord auth flow:**

1. Client opens a WebSocket to Discord Gateway.
2. HTTP/WebSocket handshake succeeds through Agent Vault.
3. Client sends an Identify payload over the established WebSocket.
4. The bot token is inside the JSON WebSocket message body, e.g. `d.token`.
5. Agent Vault currently raw-pipes WebSocket bytes after upgrade, so the placeholder is not substituted.
6. Discord closes the Gateway connection with auth failure.

## Reproduction

**Environment:**

- Agent Vault with MITM proxy enabled
- Hermes Agent gateway running under Agent Vault proxy env
- Discord configured as a Hermes messaging platform
- `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` stored as an Agent Vault credential
- Hermes configured with placeholder token: `__discord_bot_token__`

**Services configured in Agent Vault:**

```yaml
discord-api:
  host: discord.com/api/*
  auth: passthrough
  substitution:
    placeholder: __discord_bot_token__
    credential: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
    surface: header

discord-gateway:
  host: gateway.discord.gg
  auth: passthrough
  substitution:
    placeholder: __discord_bot_token__
    credential: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
    surface: header
```

**Systemd user service was configured to load Agent Vault proxy env:**

```ini
[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/root/.hermes/gateway.env
```

**Manual REST check succeeds** when the placeholder is in an HTTP header:

```bash
set -a
. /root/.hermes/gateway.env
set +a

curl --proxy-cacert /root/.agent-vault/mitm-ca.pem \
  --cacert /root/.agent-vault/mitm-ca.pem \
  -sS -o /tmp/discord_me.out -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' \
  https://discord.com/api/users/@me \
  -H 'Authorization: Bot __discord_bot_token__'

cat /tmp/discord_me.out
```

**Observed result:**

```
HTTP 200
{"id":"...","username":"bot-test", ...}
```

This confirms Agent Vault substituted the placeholder correctly for the HTTP REST request.

**Then restarting Hermes Gateway fails at the Discord Gateway stage:**

```bash
systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway
journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway -n 80 --no-pager
```

**Observed log:**

```
discord.errors.ConnectionClosed: Shard ID None WebSocket closed with 4004
```

Discord close code `4004` indicates authentication failure. This is consistent with the Identify WebSocket payload still containing the literal placeholder rather than the real token.

## Root Cause

The WebSocket proxy path upgrades the connection, then raw-copies bytes between client and upstream.

`internal/mitm/forward.go` applies substitutions only before WebSocket forwarding:

```go
brokercore.ApplySubstitutions(outReq.URL, outReq.Header, inject.Substitutions)
```

`internal/mitm/websocket.go` then pipes the WebSocket connection as bytes:

```go
pipeWebSocket(clientConn, clientBuf.Reader, upstreamConn, upstreamReader)
```

So Agent Vault never parses client→upstream WebSocket frames and cannot replace placeholders inside post-upgrade messages.

## Why this matters

Some APIs authenticate inside protocol messages rather than HTTP metadata. Discord Gateway is a concrete example: the bot token is sent in the Identify frame, not the HTTP handshake.

Without WebSocket frame substitution, users cannot keep Discord bot tokens fully inside Agent Vault when using clients that expect to place the token in the Gateway Identify payload.

## Possible Fix

Add an explicit opt-in substitution surface for WebSocket text frames, e.g.:

```yaml
substitutions:
  - key: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
    placeholder: __discord_bot_token__
    in: ["ws_text"]
```

**Implementation sketch:**

1. Add `ws_text` to the supported substitution surfaces.
2. Keep existing `path`, `query`, and `header` behavior unchanged.
3. If a matched service has `ws_text` substitutions and the request is a WebSocket upgrade:
   - Do not raw-copy client→upstream bytes.
   - Parse RFC 6455 frames from the client.
   - Unmask client frames.
   - For text messages, replace declared placeholders.
   - Re-frame data to the upstream.
   - Pass binary/control frames through correctly.
4. Apply substitutions only client→upstream, not upstream→client.
5. Add message/frame size limits.
6. Do not log resolved substitution values.
7. Disable or strip `permessage-deflate` for rewritten WebSocket connections initially, unless compression support is implemented. Rewriting compressed frames safely requires decompress/recompress.

A narrower first pass could support text frames only and reject/skip substitution when compression is negotiated.

## Security Considerations

This should be explicit opt-in. Do not scan all WebSocket traffic by default.

The substitution declaration should remain the security boundary, same as existing `path`/`query`/`header` substitutions. Operators must deliberately opt into `ws_text` for a service.

**Potential follow-up:** consider a more structured `ws_json` surface with JSON path targeting, e.g. replacing `$.d.token`, to avoid raw text replacement inside arbitrary JSON. For the Discord use case, raw text replacement of a unique placeholder is sufficient, but JSON-aware substitution may be safer long-term.

## Summary

Adds an opt-out **\"openclaw compat\"** Node preload to \`agent-vault run\`. When the wrapped command is detected as OpenClaw (either as \`openclaw\` directly, or as \`node\`/\`nodejs\` invoking an \`/openclaw/\`-pathed \`.js\` entrypoint), AV writes an embedded preload to \`~/.agent-vault/openclaw-compat.js\` and injects \`NODE_OPTIONS=--require=<path>\` into the child env. The preload patches axios in-process to fix two real bugs that previously required operators to hand-maintain a \`/root/axios-no-proxy.js\` shim plus \`NODE_OPTIONS=--require=...\` in their gateway env file.

**Net operator surface for OpenClaw + AV drops from \"1 env file + 1 axios shim + 1 systemd unit + AGENTS.md workspace doc\" to \"1 env file + 1 systemd drop-in.\"**

## The bugs

Both inherent to OpenClaw's Node dep stack; neither fixable proxy-side without invasive surgery (body-surface substitution would address one; nothing addresses the other).

1. **axios v1.x cannot speak to a TLS-wrapped HTTPS_PROXY.** It misinterprets \`https://broker:14322\` as the origin server, routes the request *to* AV as the destination, and AV's netguard correctly blocks the self-loop. Fix: \`axios.defaults.proxy = false\` so Node's \`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1\` / undici path handles the proxy natively.

2. **\`@slack/web-api\` places the bot token in the form body** when invoked with method-arg shape (\`client.auth.test({token})\`), which is exactly how Bolt's per-event \`buildAuthorizeResult\` calls it. AV's substitution surfaces are path/query/header only — body is reserved for a future version. Without intervention every Slack event silently fails with \`invalid_auth\`. Fix: an axios request interceptor that moves \`token=__placeholder__\` from the body into an \`Authorization: Bearer __placeholder__\` header, strips the body token, and recomputes Content-Length so Slack sees consistent shape.

Full incident write-ups (used as the rationale source for this PR): the operator-side debugging that motivated the feature lives in our internal incident docs; not reproduced here.

## How it works

- **\`internal/openclawcompat/preload.js\`** — \`go:embed\`'d JS. Hooks \`Module._load\` to detect when axios is required (regardless of where openclaw's \`node_modules\` is installed); on first hit, patches the singleton and wraps \`axios.create\` so every instance openclaw spawns inherits the same interceptor. Idempotent; no-op for non-axios module loads.

- **\`internal/openclawcompat/openclawcompat.go\`** — \`EnsurePreload()\` writes the embed atomically (CreateTemp → Chmod → Close → Rename in a 0700 parent dir) to \`~/.agent-vault/openclaw-compat.js\` if missing or stale. Idempotent across re-invocations.

- **\`cmd/node_compat_flag.go\`** — \`--node-compat=auto|on|off\` cobra flag. \`auto\` detects openclaw two ways: (a) bare \`openclaw\` base-name, (b) \`node\`/\`nodejs\` with a non-flag arg matching \`/openclaw/\` or \`/@openclaw/\` and ending in \`.js\`. Conservative on substring matching — \`/foo/openclawish/bar.js\` does NOT match.

- **\`cmd/run.go\`** — adds \`openclaw\` to \`knownAgents\` with skill-dir \`.agents\` (matches Codex; OpenClaw reads skills from \`~/.agents/skills/\`). Resolves ncMode at the top of \`runCmdRunE\` with \`AGENT_VAULT_NODE_COMPAT\` env-var fallback mirroring the \`AGENT_VAULT_ISOLATION\` pattern. Step 7.5 calls \`EnsurePreload()\` and \`appendNodeOptionsRequire()\` between the existing skills install and \`syscall.Exec\`. Container-isolation mode logs a stderr warning when \`--node-compat=on\` is explicitly set (the preload isn't bind-mounted into the container today — followup).

## Behavior matrix

| Invocation | Detection | Preload? |
|---|---|---|
| \`agent-vault run -- openclaw gateway start\` | auto / openclaw base-name | ✅ |
| \`agent-vault run -- /usr/bin/node /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway\` | auto / node-wrapped openclaw (the user-systemd shape) | ✅ |
| \`agent-vault run -- claude\` | auto / unrelated | ❌ |
| \`agent-vault run -- node random-script.js\` | auto / node but no openclaw path hint | ❌ |
| \`agent-vault run --node-compat=on -- anything\` | forced on | ✅ |
| \`agent-vault run --node-compat=off -- openclaw\` | forced off (escape hatch for self-patchers) | ❌ |
| \`agent-vault run --isolation=container --node-compat=on -- openclaw\` | warning to stderr; preload not in container | ❌ (with explicit warning) |

NODE_OPTIONS append-mode preserves operator-set preloads so layered patches still load; tokenized idempotency check avoids prefix-collision false-positives (e.g. an existing \`--require=/x/preload.js.bak\` no longer masks a fresh \`--require=/x/preload.js\`).

## New surface

| Surface | Value |
|---|---|
| Flag | \`--node-compat=auto\|on\|off\` on both \`agent-vault run\` and \`agent-vault vault run\` (shared factory) |
| Env var | \`AGENT_VAULT_NODE_COMPAT\` (fallback when flag not explicitly set) |
| Embedded asset | \`internal/openclawcompat/preload.js\` (CommonJS — required for \`Module._load\` hook) |
| On-disk artifact | \`~/.agent-vault/openclaw-compat.js\` (0644 in 0700 parent dir, same convention as MITM CA bundle) |
| Log line | \`agent-vault: openclaw compat preload active (<path>)\` when injection fires |
| \`knownAgents\` entry | \`{[]string{\"openclaw\"}, \"OpenClaw\", \".agents\"}\` |

## Tests

| Package | Cases |
|---|---|
| \`internal/openclawcompat\` | 5 (canonical-path write, idempotent, stale-content recovery, parent-dir 0700 perms, embed-content invariants — refuses to ship if preload doesn't reference \`axios\` + \`Module._load\`) |
| \`cmd\` (\`node_compat_flag_test.go\`) | 3 test groups, ~30 cases. Mode parser exhaustive. \`nodeCompatEnabled\` covers bare-openclaw, absolute/nested/with-args paths, all common node-wrapper shapes (linux global npm, macOS Homebrew, per-user npm, scoped \`@openclaw\` packages, with leading Node flags), plus negatives (\`node -e\`, \`random.js\`, \`hermes.js\`, substring-but-not-slash-bounded). \`appendNodeOptionsRequire\` covers no-existing, preserves-existing, preserves-operator-require, idempotent, idempotent-mid-chain, empty-existing. |

Full repo suite (\`go test ./...\`, 19 packages) green. \`node --check preload.js\` clean.

## End-to-end validation

Manually validated on two fresh DigitalOcean droplets in a shared VPC (av-broker + openclaw-box). Final-state binary:

- \`agent-vault: openclaw compat preload active\` fires from the systemd ExecStart automatically (no flag in the unit file)
- \`[slack] socket mode connected\` clean — the old \`auth.test failed at boot (invalid_auth)\` is **gone**
- \`[gateway] provider auth state pre-warmed in <N>ms\` — Anthropic brokered
- Live Slack \`@-mention\` creates a GitHub repo, bot replies with URL. AV log shows \`proxy_request\` lines for all three services with \`passthrough=false\` and 2xx/201 statuses.

## Pre-PR review

\`/simplify\` + \`/review\` + \`/security-review\` all run before opening. \`/simplify\` surfaced 15 findings; 12 fixed in-PR (commit \`ead1b3c\`), 3 documented followups. \`/security-review\` returned no high-confidence vulnerabilities — every candidate either required preexisting agent-process compromise (outside AV's threat model) or HOME control (trusted per environment).

## Followups (intentionally out of scope; will file separately)

1. **Container-mode plumbing.** Today \`--isolation=container\` + \`--node-compat=on\` emits a warning but the preload doesn't reach the container. Plumbing the bind-mount + \`BuildContainerEnv\` injection is straightforward but separate.

2. **Body-surface substitution in the broker** (the \"reserved for future version\" path in \`internal/broker/broker.go:451\`). When that lands, the preload's body→header interceptor becomes redundant — the preload would shrink to just \`axios.defaults.proxy = false\`.

3. **Code reuse:** extract a \`~/.agent-vault/\` data-dir helper (6 callers duplicate the idiom across \`pidfile\`, \`session\`, \`ca\`, \`isolation\`, \`openclawcompat\`) and promote \`ca.writeAtomic\` to a shared package (this PR reimplements the atomic-rename pattern).

4. **Unified \`knownAgentQuirks\` table.** \`tlsBridgeAutoBases\` (from the codex-tls-bridge branch, mid-merge) and \`nodeCompatAutoBases\` here are the same shape — per-agent allowlist driving per-agent workaround — but live in two unconnected maps. Could consolidate.

5. **\`Module._load\` hook removal** after axios is patched (currently stays installed for the lifetime of the child for ~zero per-require cost; minor perf).

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./...\` green
- [x] \`node --check internal/openclawcompat/preload.js\` clean
- [x] Manual deploy on two DO droplets (host isolation, user-systemd)
- [x] Live Slack \`@-mention\` exercising Anthropic + GitHub round-trip; bot replies; AV proxy log shows substitution firing
- [ ] CI green (will surface on PR)

title: feat: external credential stores (Infisical integration)
body:
## Summary

Adds a second credential-source mode for vaults. When `INFISICAL_URL` plus one auth-method env-var group is set, operators can create vaults with `--credential-store=infisical`. A background syncer polls Infisical at a per-vault cadence, encrypts the snapshot with the broker DEK, and writes it into the existing `credentials` table. The proxy hot path is unchanged across kinds.

For external-store vaults, Infisical stays the source of truth:
- `POST` / `DELETE /v1/credentials` return `409 external_credential_store`.
- Proposals with `credentials[]` are rejected at create and approve time. Service-only proposals still work.
- The credential-store kind is set at create time and is immutable.

Vault creation is atomic. The handler probes Infisical first; only if the fetch succeeds does it commit the vault row, the credential-store config, the initial encrypted snapshot, and the creator's admin grant in a single SQL transaction. If the probe fails nothing is persisted. Outages are serve-stale; `last_sync_status` surfaces in the CLI and Web UI.

## Surface area

- **CLI:** new flags on `vault create` (`--credential-store`, `--infisical-project-id`, `--infisical-environment`, `--infisical-path`, `--poll-interval-seconds`) and new `vault credential-store show <name>` / `vault credential-store sync <name>` subcommands.
- **HTTP:** `POST /v1/vaults` accepts an optional `credential_store` block; `GET /v1/vaults` and `GET /v1/vaults/{name}/context` surface the kind plus sync health; new `GET /v1/instance/credential-stores` for the modal picker.
- **Web UI:** create-vault modal adds the picker + Infisical config fields; vault cards show a status pill; Credentials tab becomes read-only for external vaults; Settings tab gains a credential-store info panel; Proposals tab shows a banner.
- **Schema:** migration 047 adds `vault_credential_stores`. Cached credentials live in the existing `credentials` table (same DEK, same scheme).

## Auth methods supported

Universal Auth, Kubernetes Auth, AWS IAM Auth, GCP IAM Auth, GCP ID Token Auth, LDAP Auth. Detection is env-var-driven in a deterministic priority order; multiple complete groups log a warning and pick the highest priority. See `docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx` for the full env-var table.

Azure and OCI are intentionally **not** in V1 — the SDK requires fields not exposed via env, so dispatching them with empty args would silently build invalid upstream signatures. Re-add once we can wire the missing config.

## Security notes

- Cached values use the same AES-256-GCM scheme as built-in credentials (same DEK, fresh nonce per row). At-rest threat model is unchanged: an attacker with the DB but not the DEK sees only ciphertext.
- The Infisical SDK is constructed with `CacheExpiryInSeconds: 0` so it never holds plaintext across calls. Plaintext lives in memory only for the lifetime of a single proxied request (the existing per-request decrypt memo).
- Recommended posture: Infisical machine identity scoped read-only. Agent Vault never writes back.
- Startup probe wraps the initial SDK login in a 10s timeout so a slow Infisical can't hang `agent-vault server` boot. Existing vaults continue serving stale on failure.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` clean (new tests in `internal/store`, `internal/server`, `internal/infisical`).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npm run build` clean.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end (operator side):
  - [ ] Start with `INFISICAL_URL` + universal-auth creds; create an Infisical-backed vault and verify the initial snapshot lands.
  - [ ] Create the same vault with a bogus project ID; expect 400 with `infisical_fetch_failed` and confirm `vault list` does not show it.
  - [ ] `agent-vault credential set FOO=bar --vault=demo` returns `409 external_credential_store`.
  - [ ] Add a service to the vault, point an upstream call through `HTTPS_PROXY`, confirm the cached credential is injected.
  - [ ] Rotate a secret in Infisical, wait ≥ poll interval, retry the upstream call.
  - [ ] Kill Infisical, confirm proxy keeps serving stale and `last_sync_status` flips to `error`.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end (web UI):
  - [ ] Create-vault modal renders Infisical fields when `INFISICAL_URL` is configured server-side.
  - [ ] Vault card shows the kind pill with a colored status dot.
  - [ ] Credentials tab on an external vault hides Add/Edit/Delete and shows the read-only banner.
  - [ ] Settings tab shows the credential-store panel with poll interval + last sync info.
  - [ ] Proposals tab shows the info banner on external vaults.
